assumptions.ruleset: Gathering Storm with every expansion and the Leader Pass
assumptions.map: Continents or Pangaea, standard size, 8 civilizations
assumptions.notes: Turn numbers are Standard-speed scaffolding; the site rescales them for other speeds and difficulties. Trajan has one persona and that is the one planned here.

verdict.one_line: Settle eight to ten cities before turn 80 on free Monuments, free Trading Posts and free roads, choose by turn 60 whether the Legions take a neighbour or the cities take Campuses, and spend the Culture lead on the civics that serve that choice.
verdict.why: Trajan's Column puts a Monument in every city on the turn it is founded, and All Roads Lead to Rome gives each one a Trading Post and a road home, so a Roman city is productive and connected from turn one instead of turn fifteen. That is a settling bonus and a Culture bonus, and neither of them wins anything by itself; the Culture buys civics and the civics buy governments and policies that have to point somewhere. Science is the default because a wide empire with a Campus in every city is the thing this kit builds fastest and the Legion window is short, but a neighbour within twelve tiles at turn 50 makes the Legion push the better opening, which is why Domination is the second direction and not Culture.

must_have: Land for eight cities within trade range of the capital, since the free roads and the Trading Posts only connect cities in range.
Fresh water or a Mountain beside at least half the city sites, because the Bath has the Aqueduct's placement rule.
prefer: A rival capital within twelve tiles for the Legion option.
Plains Hills for Legion Production and Mines for Apprenticeship.
Pamukkale or Chocolate Hills in reach; Amenities and Production are what a wide Rome runs short of.
map_check.no_go: A small island or a start with room for three cities. Every Roman bonus is paid per city founded; three cities is three Monuments and the kit is finished by turn 40.
map_check.fallback: If the land is short, settle it anyway and take the Domination direction at turn 60: Legions need Iron, so settle toward a source, and the free roads move them to the border, and the neighbour's land becomes Roman cities with their own free Monuments on capture.

kit_levers.name: Trajan's Column
kit_levers.buys: A free Monument in every city founded or captured in the Ancient era, or the era-appropriate City Center building later.
kit_levers.exploit: Found cities instead of building Monuments, and found them early, because a city founded in the Ancient era gets a Monument while one founded later gets less. The Culture is the civic lead that the direction decision spends; a captured city gets the free building too, so conquest in the Classical era is still inside the ability.

kit_levers.name: All Roads Lead to Rome
kit_levers.buys: A free Trading Post in every city, automatic roads to new cities within trade range of the capital, and extra Gold on Trade Routes that pass through Roman cities.
kit_levers.exploit: Domestic Trade Routes pass through Trading Posts the moment they leave the capital, so the first Traders pay more than anyone else's. The roads move Settlers, Builders and Legions to the frontier at road speed, which is why the plan settles outward in a chain rather than a scatter.

kit_levers.name: Legion
kit_levers.buys: A Swordsman replacement with 40 Combat Strength that needs Iron like the Swordsman and carries one build charge for a Roman Fort, a road or clearing a feature.
kit_levers.exploit: The Domination option: six Legions under Oligarchy take a Classical capital before Walls, and the charge builds a Fort on the border afterward. On the Science option two Legions escort Settlers and clear the camps, and their charges clear features for districts.

kit_levers.name: Bath
kit_levers.buys: An Aqueduct replacement with extra Housing and an Amenity, placed like an Aqueduct beside the City Center and a water source or Mountain.
kit_levers.exploit: A wide empire's limit is Amenities and Housing, not land. A Bath in every river or lake city removes both limits for one district, triggers the Military Engineering Eureka as an Aqueduct would, and gives the Industrial Zone beside it adjacency.

kit_levers.name: Optimus Princeps
kit_levers.buys: Trajan respects civilizations with a lot of territory and looks down on those with little.
kit_levers.exploit: Only matters for AI Trajan: a wide Rome of your own keeps him friendly, which frees the Legions for a smaller neighbour.

options.when_it_fits: Eight or more city sites are settled or claimed by turn 60 and no neighbour is both close and weak. A Campus in every city, Baths for the Housing to staff them, and the Culture lead spent on Recorded History, The Enlightenment and the Science governments out-researches any normal empire; nothing in the kit expires on this path.

A rival capital is within twelve tiles by road at turn 50 and has no Walls. Six Legions and a Battering Ram take it and one more city before Medieval Walls, each capture gets its own free building, and the empire that results is the Science empire with two more cities. If the window is missed, this option closes until Renaissance siege.

Two Cultural city-states are met by turn 40 and the capital has already landed a Classical wonder. Ten Monuments make the civic tree fast and ten Theater Squares make Tourism wide, but nothing in the kit makes Great Works or Tourism cheaper, so take this only when the map has already handed over the pieces.

direction.commit_test: At turn 90 look at what the Culture bought: if the last three civics were Recorded History, Drama and Poetry and Theology for the Science or Culture path, or Military Tradition, Military Training and Political Philosophy for Oligarchy, the direction is chosen. If they were whatever came next on the tree, the lead is being banked and the plan has failed its own test.

phases.name: Settle in a chain
phases.objective: Found four cities in a chain outward from the capital so each gets a free Monument, a Trading Post and a road, pick City Patron Goddess, and scout the nearest rival for the turn 60 decision.

build_order.why: Finds the city chain and the nearest rival; Writing on the first meeting.
Second Warrior escorts the first Settler and clears the nearest camp for Bronze Working.
No Monument to build, so the Settler is the second item; the second city is founded by turn 18.
Archery Eureka on a camp scout and a defender while the Warriors escort.
Third city on the road the second one pulled out of the capital.
A Mine for The Wheel, a Quarry for Masonry, a Farm on a resource for Irrigation.
Fourth city; the capital has Housing to spare and Colonization is slotted by now.
Escort for the fourth Settler; it upgrades to a Legion at Iron Working.

research.note: Mines for The Wheel and Apprenticeship; Bronze Working next.
Three camp kills from the escort Warriors; Iron Working and the Legion are behind it.
Slinger kill at the first camp; Archers behind the Legions later.
A Quarry gives the Eureka; the Pyramids and Ancient Walls.
A Mine on a resource; Water Mills in the river cities.
The Scout meets a rival; Campuses are the Science direction.

civics.note: God King for the pantheon and Discipline for the escorts.
Three improvements from the first Builder; Ilkum for the next Builders.
Six population across two cities; Colonization for Settlers three and four.
The first Trade Route; Caravansaries and the Roman road Gold.
The first district gives the Inspiration; the Monuments make this arrive early.

policies.why: City Patron Goddess by turn 22; swap it out the turn after.
Warriors beat camp units while escorting Settlers.
+50% Production toward Settlers; the chain runs on it until turn 80.

pantheon.why: Every new city builds its first district a quarter faster, and this empire founds more cities than anyone.

city_states.why: The first envoy is Production toward districts in the capital, and the capital builds Settlers and then a Campus.
Loyalty per Encampment building; a wide empire's far cities need it and the Domination direction needs it more.

checkpoints.test: Two cities founded, each with its free Monument, the pantheon taken and a rival capital located?
checkpoints.pass: Keep the chain going; Settler three is in the queue.
checkpoints.fail: A second city after turn 22 means the Settler came too late in the queue; move the third Settler ahead of the Builder. No rival located by turn 30 means the Scout went the wrong way; send a Warrior the other way.

checkpoints.test: Four cities founded, all connected by road, and the Culture rate at or above the top rival's?
checkpoints.pass: Enter the Legion phase; the direction decision is twenty turns away.
checkpoints.fail: Three cities is acceptable with the fourth Settler walking; the roads not connecting means a city was founded outside trade range, and the next ones go closer. Culture below a rival with four Monuments means the Monuments are not being worked around; check that no city is building a Monument it already has.

tasks.text: Settle on the spot or one move to a river or Mountain; the Bath needs one of them later.
Scout toward the nearest rival capital and note its distance by road; the turn 60 decision is this number.
Second city founded four to six tiles out; confirm the road appears and the Monument is there.
Found City Patron Goddess, or Religious Settlements if the land is wide enough to want the free Settler more.
Fourth city founded on the chain; stop building Monuments anywhere, ever.

checkpoints.fail: No direction at turn 60 is the shape's failure. Decide by distance: a rival within twelve tiles with no Walls is Domination, anything else is Science. checkpoints.test: Eight cities, a government, Baths in the river cities, and the queues showing the direction: six Legions and a Ram at the border, or a Campus in six cities with Libraries?

decision_triggers.name: Neighbour in Legion range
decision_triggers.if: At turn 50 a rival capital is within twelve tiles by road and has no Walls.
decision_triggers.then: Choose Domination at turn 60. Six Legions under Oligarchy and a Battering Ram take it by turn 90; each capture gets a free building and the empire continues as the Science empire afterward.

decision_triggers.name: Civics drifting
decision_triggers.if: At any era checkpoint the last three civics were not on the chosen direction's path.
decision_triggers.then: The Monuments are being banked. Re-pick the civic queue today toward the direction's government and policies, and note it as a near-miss on the plan.

decision_triggers.name: Amenities first
decision_triggers.if: Three or more cities show negative Amenities.
decision_triggers.then: Stop settling, build Arenas, buy a luxury, and send envoys to Buenos Aires. Rome's limit is Amenities, and the roads bring rebels as fast as Legions.

decision_triggers.name: Walls before the Legions
decision_triggers.if: The Legion target builds Ancient Walls before turn 85.
decision_triggers.then: Bring a Battering Ram and keep going; Legions at 44 with a Ram still break Ancient Walls. Medieval Walls close the window; switch to Science and come back with Bombards if ever.

abort.trigger: Turn 150 with no direction committed: no capital taken, no Campus in half the cities, no Theater Square outside the capital, and a civic tree picked in order.
actions: Pick the direction the empire is already closest to; with ten Roman cities that is almost always Science. Commit fully; Linear leaders lose by drifting, not by collapsing.
Reroute the civic queue to Recorded History, The Enlightenment and Class Struggle today.
Put a Campus in every city without one before any other district.

fail_state: Turn 200 with twelve comfortable cities, Monuments and Baths everywhere, a civic tree an era ahead of everyone and nothing to show for it: no capital taken, Campuses in four cities, no Spaceport site, and the Culture lead spent on whatever civic came next. Rome has out-settled the map and converted none of it, and the ability has nothing left to add.
common_mistakes: Building Monuments. Every Roman city already has one; the queue slot is a Settler or a Builder.
Founding cities outside trade range of the capital. They get no road and no connection, and the chain breaks there.
Treating the Culture lead as a score. It buys civics; if the civics are not pointing at a victory, it buys nothing.
Settling until the land ends instead of until Amenities end. Rome's real cap is happiness, and free roads carry rebellion as easily as Legions.
Researching Iron Working with no Iron source in reach. Legions need Iron; six Legions by turn 80 is the whole Domination option and it closes with Medieval Walls.
